request.text:
A: I set a bowl out for the old goblin woman. Silly. Habit. Somebody ought to mourn her.
<long pause>
A: Stew's going up the hill by the potful. Don't look at me like that. Hungry's hungry.
<long pause>
A: Found them under the bridge, behind the pilings. Too weak to run with the rest. Neither of them's bigger than Pip, Halden.
<long pause>
A: She bit me twice on the way here. I'd call that healthy.
<long pause>
A: I'll take the little ones home tonight. Pip can teach them to steal bread properly.
<long pause>
A: Colder everywhere. The dockside fields froze the night you left with it. Folk are blaming the weather. I'm not.
<long pause>
A: I'm not saying you were wrong. I'm saying somebody's paying for it, and it's not the ones who decided.
<long pause>
A: Still there. I send them soup at midnight. One of them cried, last week. Said the glow reminds him of his mother's kitchen.
<long pause>
A: Town's warmer for it. For now. Everyone knows it won't last, so nobody says so.
<long pause>
A: Next to nothing, apiece. Everyone's warm and cheerful, and half of them can't remember what they had for breakfast.
<long pause>
A: I won't buy one. I've lost enough to Gran's old shard. I'll not hurry the rest along.
<long pause>
A: <practical, warm, quick but clear Mood: sad.> Bree poured one for the goblin grandmother tonight. Nobody asked why. Nobody drank it.
<long pause>
A: <practical, warm, quick but clear Mood: happy.> We send stew up the hill now. Bree says hungry is hungry, whatever its ears look like.
<long pause>
A: <practical, warm, quick but clear Mood: idle.> Bree's hearth is the warmest room in town again. Funny how that's starting to matter.
<long pause>
A: <practical, warm, quick but clear Mood: idle.> Folk keep coming in to shout about the mayor. Then they stay for the soup.
<long pause>
A: <practical, warm, quick but clear Mood: idle.> Every hearth in town has a new shard. Bree won't buy one. Says she's forgotten enough.
<long pause>
A: My hearth's the warmest in town again. People keep asking me why. I keep telling them it's the stew.
<long pause>
A: You'll want feeding. Sit. I heard what happened on the bridge. I'm not asking, and you're not telling. Not tonight.
<long pause>
A: Half the town says you've gone soft, and the other half is eating better for it. I know which half I'm in.
<long pause>
B: <Elderly goblin matriarch: low female contralto, husky dry rasp and age-creak; measured, wary, quietly commanding, with tired warmth. Mood: idle.> Valley people. Say what you came to say, or go back down the hill.
<long pause>
B: <Elderly goblin matriarch: low female contralto, husky dry rasp and age-creak; measured, wary, quietly commanding, with tired warmth. Mood: idle.> You came back up the hill. Not many valley people do that twice.
<long pause>
B: <Elderly goblin matriarch: low female contralto, husky dry rasp and age-creak; measured, wary, quietly commanding, with tired warmth. Mood: idle.> Fed. For now. The little ones have stopped crying in the night. That is a sound I had forgotten.
<long pause>
B: <Elderly goblin matriarch: low female contralto, husky dry rasp and age-creak; measured, wary, quietly commanding, with tired warmth. Mood: idle.> With my grandson. Vorga thinks a bargain is a defeat. He took the angriest of our young and went east. He will be someone's problem.
<long pause>
B: <Elderly goblin matriarch: low female contralto, husky dry rasp and age-creak; measured, wary, quietly commanding, with tired warmth. Mood: idle.> Anything else, valley people? The fire is small, and I am old.
<long pause>
B: <Elderly goblin matriarch: low female contralto, husky dry rasp and age-creak; measured, wary, quietly commanding, with tired warmth. Mood: idle.> Go well. Walk loud on the path, so the archers know it is you.
